newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Gas Natural 96 profit seen at 48 bln ptas.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Gas Natural 96 profit seen at 48 bln ptas.

text.p: The net profit for Spain's gas company Gas Natural in 1996 was around 48 billion pesetas, the firm's chairman Pedro Duran said on Thursday.
"Gas Natural profits have gone from 10 billion pesetas five years ago to 48 billion in 1996," Duran told a luncheon meeting of the Spanish Energy Club.
He said turnover would be around 350 billion pesetas.
The profit figures are similar to those he forecast on December 9 when he said the firm would earn 50 billion in 1996.

Duran said there was a lot of room for growth in the use of gas in Spain, because restrictive policies in the 1970s under the dictatorship of Francisco Franco held the Spanish industry back in comparison to the rest of Europe.

He said the use of natural gas as an "alternative" fuel to produce electricity was growing and would be at 20 billion therms in 1997. Five percent of the country's gas consumption goes to produce electricity at the moment and he hoped it would grow to 20 percent.
Looking ahead to 1998 and 1999, Duran said there were contacts with electricity utilities to reach accords on the use of natural gas.
But he did not see the possibility of a second operator entering the market.
"There are companies that want to be a second operator. Very good, but this is what we call virtual reality," Duran said.
Gas Natural shares were trading down 220 pesetas at 33,140.
